main.title: World Wide Web
main.summary: Tim Berners-Lee conceived the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989 as a linked information system.

cards.heading: World Wide Web
cards.text: Tim Berners-Lee conceived the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989 as a linked information system. A document could contain a hyperlink leading directly to another resource, making connected information easier to navigate. Web servers supplied pages to browsers, using HTTP to exchange them and URLs to locate them. HTML gave authors a common way to arrange text and incorporate images, sound and video. CERN made the Web software freely available in 1993, helping publishing and following links become an everyday way to share information over the Internet.

main.title: Hubble Space Telescope
main.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope (HST or Hubble) is a space telescope that was launched into low Earth orbit in 1990 and remains in operation.

cards.heading: Hubble Space Telescope
cards.text:
The Hubble Space Telescope was launched into low Earth orbit in 1990. Named after astronomer Edwin Hubble, it belongs to NASA's Great Observatories. The Space Telescope Science Institute selects its targets and processes the observations, while the Goddard Space Flight Center controls the spacecraft.

Its 2.4-metre mirror and five main instruments observe ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared light. Orbiting above the atmospheric distortion affecting telescopes on Earth allows Hubble to capture detailed images of distant objects. Its observations have supported major developments in astrophysics, including measurements of the universe's rate of expansion.

main.title: Twin Peaks
main.subtitle: A murder investigation uncovers a town of secrets and strange connections
main.summary: David Lynch and Mark Frost's Twin Peaks begins with the discovery of Laura Palmer's body in a small northwestern town. Kyle MacLachlan plays FBI agent Dale Cooper, whose arrival brings a fresh manner of investigation to the local police. The series premiered on ABC in the United States on 8 April 1990, combining a murder mystery with the private lives of the people around it.

cards.heading: The original 1990 series
cards.text: David Lynch and Mark Frost's Twin Peaks begins with the discovery of Laura Palmer's body in a small northwestern town. Kyle MacLachlan plays FBI agent Dale Cooper, whose arrival brings a fresh manner of investigation to the local police. The series premiered on ABC in the United States on 8 April 1990, combining a murder mystery with the private lives of the people around it.

cards.heading: The routines around a mystery
cards.text: Cooper's curiosity reaches beyond conventional evidence. Dreams, intuition and apparently incidental details become part of the investigation, while conversations in diners, homes and workplaces reveal different versions of Laura's life. The town's familiar routines make the disturbances more unsettling. Coffee, pie and affectionate eccentricity exist beside exploitation and fear, and a character who first appears comic may later occupy a much darker part of the story.

cards.heading: A town held together by mood
cards.text: Angelo Badalamenti's music gives those changes of mood a strong continuity, moving between warmth, melancholy and threat. Lynch and Frost let the continuing mystery share time with romances and local schemes, drawing on television melodrama while introducing images and rhythms that do not resolve neatly into explanation. The weekly broadcast made uncertainty a shared subject of conversation. Its original two-season run left a world that Lynch and Frost would return to in later work.

main.title: Dances with Wolves
main.subtitle: A frontier posting becomes an encounter with another community
main.summary: Kevin Costner directs and stars in Dances with Wolves, the story of a Union officer whose isolated frontier posting brings him into contact with a Lakota community. Adapted by Michael Blake from his novel, the film opened in limited release on 9 November 1990. Its long encounters and attention to language give the officer's changing relationships room to develop.

cards.heading: A solitary posting
cards.text: Kevin Costner directs and stars in Dances with Wolves, the story of a Union officer whose isolated frontier posting brings him into contact with a Lakota community. Adapted by Michael Blake from his novel, the film opened in limited release on 9 November 1990. Its long encounters and attention to language give the officer's changing relationships room to develop.

cards.heading: Learning to speak and listen
cards.text: John Dunbar initially meets his neighbours through suspicion, observation and awkward attempts to communicate. Friendship with Kicking Bird and the help of Stands With a Fist make further exchanges possible. Visits, shared activities and the buffalo hunt gradually replace his solitary routine. Dunbar keeps a written account of these experiences, so the film traces a change in how he describes the people around him as well as how he behaves toward them.

cards.heading: A frontier seen differently
cards.text: The use of Lakota dialogue with subtitles gives the community conversations that extend beyond the newcomer. Dean Semler's landscape photography and John Barry's score create a broad setting for the more patient scenes of contact. The story remains organised around Dunbar's perspective, but the return of the United States Army makes the consequences of that perspective sharper: the people he has come to know are approached through assumptions he can no longer accept.

main.title: Gulf War
main.summary: The Gulf War was an armed conflict between Iraq and a 42-country coalition led by the United States in response to Saddam Hussein invading neighboring Kuwait on 2 August 1990.

cards.heading: Gulf War
cards.text:
The Gulf War was an armed conflict between Iraq and a 42-country coalition led by the United States in response to Saddam Hussein invading neighboring Kuwait on 2 August 1990. The coalition's efforts were in two phases: Operation Desert Shield, which marked the military buildup from August 1990 to January 1991; and Operation Desert Storm, from the bombing campaign against Iraq on 17 January until the American-led liberation of Kuwait on 28 February.

The invasion of Kuwait was met with immediate international condemnation. The UN Security Council demanded Iraq's immediate withdrawal and imposed a total embargo on products from Iraq and Kuwait. A coalition began a military buildup in the Persian Gulf region. The broadest military alliance since World War II, its largest contributors were the US, Saudi Arabia, the United Kingdom, and Egypt.

main.title: Mediterraneo
main.subtitle: Eight soldiers lose contact with the war around them
main.summary: Gabriele Salvatores' Mediterraneo sends eight Italian soldiers to a small Greek island during the Second World War. Cut off from their superiors, the men gradually build a daily life with the inhabitants they were sent to control. Released in 1991, the film uses an isolated setting and an ensemble cast to explore the attraction of stepping outside the roles assigned by war.

cards.heading: A unit left behind
cards.text: Gabriele Salvatores' Mediterraneo sends eight Italian soldiers to a small Greek island during the Second World War. Cut off from their superiors, the men gradually build a daily life with the inhabitants they were sent to control. Released in 1991, the film uses an isolated setting and an ensemble cast to explore the attraction of stepping outside the roles assigned by war.

cards.heading: An island becomes everyday life
cards.text: A lost ship and a broken radio leave the unit waiting for instructions that do not arrive. Patrols and military routines give way to friendships, games, work and romance. The soldiers' different temperaments emerge as they discover what they want from this unexpected interval. The island's residents have lives and needs of their own, so the occupation becomes an uneasy shared existence. News from outside eventually forces the men to confront how far their private refuge has drifted from events elsewhere.

cards.heading: The sound of a refuge
cards.text: Giancarlo Bigazzi and Marco Falagiani's score gives the island a distinctive sound through acoustic instruments including bouzouki, santur and local wind and percussion colours. Its recurring themes accompany the passing days as the characters become accustomed to their surroundings. Vincenzo Monteleone's screenplay keeps their relationships at the centre of the film. Mediterraneo won the 1992 foreign-language Oscar, bringing international attention to Salvatores' ensemble and its story of escape, belonging and the difficulty of returning.

main.title: Nevermind
main.summary: Nevermind is the second studio album by American rock band Nirvana, released on September 24, 1991, by DGC Records.

cards.heading: Nevermind
cards.text:
Nevermind is the second studio album by American rock band Nirvana, released on September 24, 1991, by DGC Records. Produced by Butch Vig, Nevermind features a more polished, radio-friendly sound than the band's prior work. It was recorded at Sound City Studios in Van Nuys, California, and Smart Studios in Madison, Wisconsin, in May and June 1991, and mastered that August at the Mastering Lab in Hollywood, California. Nevermind was Nirvana's first album to feature drummer Dave Grohl.

Written primarily by frontman Kurt Cobain, the album's lyrical themes include social alienation and frustration, anti-establishment and feminist views, and relationship issues; these were more sensitive compared to what was common in mainstream rock music at the time. Musically rooted in grunge and alternative rock, the album also features acoustic ballads and punk-inspired hard rock.

main.title: Dolby Digital
main.summary: Dolby Digital is a family of audio-compression technologies developed by Dolby Laboratories, first used to deliver digital cinema sound from 35mm film prints.

cards.heading: Dolby Digital
cards.text:
Dolby Digital is a family of audio-compression technologies developed by Dolby Laboratories. Originally known as Dolby Stereo Digital, it first delivered digital cinema sound from 35mm film prints. It later reached television, satellite radio, streaming services, DVDs, Blu-ray discs and game consoles.

The original AC-3 codec uses multichannel audio coding based on the modified discrete cosine transform, or MDCT. This developed from the discrete cosine transform proposed by Nasir Ahmed in 1972 for image compression, adapted into the MDCT by J. P. Princen, A. W. Johnson and Alan B. Bradley at the University of Surrey in 1987.

main.title: Disneyland Paris opens
main.subtitle: Euro Disneyland welcomes its first visitors
main.summary: Euro Disneyland opened to the public at Marne-la-Vallée, east of Paris, on 12 April 1992.

cards.heading: Euro Disneyland welcomes its first visitors
cards.text: Euro Disneyland opened on April 12, 1992, at Marne-la-Vallée, east of Paris, after a weekend of previews and celebrations. Disney's first European resort began with one theme park, hotels and the Festival Disney entertainment district. A 1987 agreement with French authorities established the framework, and construction began in 1988. The destination later became known as Disneyland Paris, with Walt Disney Studios Park joining it as a second theme park in 2002.

main.title: Jurassic Park
main.summary: Steven Spielberg's Jurassic Park opened in 1993, adapting Michael Crichton's novel about a wildlife park populated by recreated dinosaurs.

cards.heading: Jurassic Park
cards.text: Steven Spielberg's Jurassic Park opened in 1993, adapting Michael Crichton's novel about a wildlife park populated by recreated dinosaurs. When power and security systems fail on Isla Nublar, visiting experts and children must escape the animals. Sam Neill, Laura Dern and Jeff Goldblum play members of the group confronting John Hammond's project. Crichton worked on the screenplay before David Koepp produced the final draft, reducing exposition and changing characters. Filming took place in California and Hawaii in 1992, followed by post-production that continued while Spielberg was making Schindler's List in Poland.
